methods.title: Categories 1 and 2: supplier-specific product emission factors and supplier-allocated emissions
methods.formula: product factor: kg CO2e = quantity bought x supplier factor (kg CO2e per unit); allocated total: kg CO2e = supplier kg CO2e (metric tons x 1000) x numerator / denominator (rounded half-even to 12 dp), or x 1 when the supplier allocated it

methods.title: Category 3 activity C: generation of electricity lost in transmission and distribution (eGRID2023 rev2)
methods.formula: loss MWh = consumed MWh x GGL / (1 - GGL) (interconnect grid gross loss, eGRID GGL23; quotient rounded half-even to 12 dp); kg gas = loss MWh x subregion total output rate (lb/MWh) x 0.45359237; kg CO2e = CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265

methods.title: Category 3 activity A: upstream (cradle-to-gate) of purchased fuels (NETL 2024 natural gas supply chain; CA-GREET3.0 petroleum and propane pathways)
methods.formula: natural gas: kg CO2e = MMBtu (HHV; the Scope 1 engine's rules: therms x 0.1, MMBtu as stated, or volume x the heat content stated on the bill, a division by 100 or 1,000 listed) x 9.284491503056 (NETL production through distribution 8.8 g CO2e/MJ x 1055.05585262 MJ/MMBtu / 1000); liquid fuels: kg CO2e = gallons (as Scope 1: measured, or purchases + opening - closing tank) x CARB LCFS energy density (MJ/gal, LHV) x CA-GREET3.0 upstream carbon intensity (Total - Tailpipe, g CO2e/MJ, LHV) x 0.001

methods.title: Category 3 activity B: upstream (cradle-to-gate) of fuels used to generate purchased electricity (eGRID2023 rev2 heat input; NETL 2024 natural gas)
methods.formula: kg CO2e = consumed MWh (kWh x 0.001) x U(s); U(s) = sum over mapped fuels f of round12(heat input(s, f) MMBtu / net generation(s) MWh) x upstream factor(f) kg CO2e per MMBtu (HHV); gas 8.229435650436; oil round12(UP_ulsd x ED_ulsd x 0.001 / 0.138); coal (mine methane only) round12(43.6 x 10^9 / (594,155 x 1000 x 20.100)) = 3.650822140444; memo: unmapped fossil MMBtu = MWh x round12(unmapped fossil heat input / net generation); coal MMBtu = MWh x round12(coal heat input / net generation); screening memo (outside totals): coal MMBtu x 5.0 x 0.45359237 to coal MMBtu x (12.2 x 1055.05585262 x 0.001 - 3.650822140444) kg CO2e of omitted coal mining energy and transport CO2

methods.title: Category 3 activity C, upstream part: upstream (cradle-to-gate) of fuels used to generate electricity lost in transmission and distribution (eGRID2023 rev2; NETL 2024)
methods.formula: loss MWh = consumed MWh x GGL / (1 - GGL) exactly as category 3C (quotient rounded half-even to 12 dp); kg CO2e = loss MWh x U(s), U(s) as category 3B

methods.title: Categories 4 and 9: upstream and downstream transportation, distance-based (Hub Table 8)
methods.formula: kg CO2 = activity x CO2 factor (kg/unit); kg CH4 and N2O = activity x factor (g/unit) x 0.001; kg CO2e = CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265. activity = vehicle-miles for a dedicated vehicle, short ton-miles for a shared vehicle (tonne-km x 1000 / (0.45359237 x 2000 x 1.609344), rounded half-even to 12 dp)

methods.title: Categories 5 and 12: waste generated in operations and end-of-life of sold products (Hub Table 9)
methods.formula: short tons = short tons, lb / 2000, kg / (0.45359237 x 2000), or metric tons x 1000 / (0.45359237 x 2000) (quotient rounded half-even to 12 dp); kg CO2e = short tons x factor (metric tons CO2e per short ton) x 1000

methods.title: Category 6: business travel, distance-based (Hub Table 10)
methods.formula: kg CO2 = activity x CO2 factor (kg/unit); kg CH4 and N2O = activity x factor (g/unit) x 0.001; kg CO2e = CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265. Cars and motorcycles per vehicle-mile; rail, bus and air per passenger-mile; air haul from the one-way segment distance (< 300, 300 to < 2300, >= 2300 miles)

methods.title: Category 7: employee commuting, distance-based (Hub Table 10)
methods.formula: kg CO2 = activity x CO2 factor (kg/unit); kg CH4 and N2O = activity x factor (g/unit) x 0.001; kg CO2e = CO2 + CH4 x 28 + N2O x 265. Cars and motorcycles per vehicle-mile (a shared car counts once); rail and bus per passenger-mile

methods.title: Categories 1 and 2, and the spend-based fallback for 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9: EPA Supply Chain GHG Emission Factors v1.3 (2022 USD)
methods.formula: kg CO2e = amount (USD) x factor (kg CO2e per 2022 USD, purchaser price, published with or without margins for the 2017 NAICS-6 code) x r; r = I2022 / I(dollar year) of the BEA GDP implicit price deflator (FRED A191RD3A086NBEA), rounded half-even to 12 dp and listed; no r for 2022 dollars

disclosures.text: Waste is reported as CO2e calculated by EPA with IPCC AR4 GWPs, with no split by gas; other Scope 3 figures use AR5.
Waste excludes avoided emissions from recycling or energy recovery.
Air travel uses an average passenger factor; cabin class is not differentiated.
CA-GREET3.0 values (lookup tables of 2018) and the LCFS energy densities of the 2019 regulation text are used. The LCFS moved to CA-GREET4.0 from 1 July 2025; its values are not loaded here.
Capital goods count the full cradle-to-gate emissions of their acquisition cost in the year of acquisition; they are not depreciated.

Upstream of coal-fired generation counts coal mine methane only: EPA’s U.S. greenhouse gas inventory gives 43.6 million metric tons CO2e of methane from coal mining in 2022 (IPCC AR5 GWPs; active underground mines net of methane recovered, surface mines and post-mining; abandoned mines excluded), divided by EIA’s 2022 U.S. coal production (594,155 thousand short tons x 20.100 MMBtu per short ton, higher heating value): 3.650822140444 kg CO2e per MMBtu of coal. The energy used to mine coal and the CO2 of transporting it are not included, so the line is partial and this cannot be documented away as an exclusion; each line states its coal heat input (MMBtu, a memo outside every total). This is never treated as zero.

Screening estimate, outside every total: the coal mining energy and transport CO2 that this line does not count is shown as a range (two memo items). Low end: the National Petroleum Council’s 2011 coal upstream combustion, 5.0 lb CO2e per MMBtu (IPCC AR4 GWPs, 1997 coal data). High end: Abrahams et al. (2015) coal upstream, 12.2 g CO2e per MJ, less the coal mine methane already counted. Both are older studies, neither states its heating value, and Abrahams models the methane GWP as a distribution that is not an IPCC set, so this only sizes the gap; it is never a figure, and the gap is never treated as zero.

Each grid-loss (3C) or energy-resold (3D) combustion line is paired with its upstream line for the same record, so together they cover the life cycle of that electricity; the combustion line’s “upstream not included” note no longer applies.
Spend uses EPA factors with margins: cradle to shelf at purchaser prices, including the transport, wholesale and retail margins of the goods bought.

The category’s data-quality label is capped at fair because some of its activity is not quantified (held or pending lines, or a partial boundary that is not a documented exclusion). The methodology says why.
An estimate: spend not in 2022 dollars was converted with the BEA GDP implicit price deflator, an economy-wide index; EPA recommends commodity-specific price indexes.
Some activity data is estimated; each estimated record states its basis.
Excluded without a magnitude: the assessment gives neither an estimated magnitude in t CO2e nor the reason it cannot be quantified.

Excluded without relevance criteria: the assessment does not record which Scope 3 Standard Table 6.1 criteria (size, influence, risk, stakeholders, outsourcing, sector guidance or other) the company considered.
EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, edition last modified 15 January 2025 (Tables 8, 9 and 10); EPA eGRID2023 (revision 2) subregion emission rates and grid gross loss.
EPA Supply Chain GHG Emission Factors v1.3 use U.S. greenhouse gas data for 2022 in 2022 dollars, with IPCC AR5 GWPs applied by EPA (CO2e only, not split by gas).

Other fossil fuels burned for electricity in this subregion (eGRID “other fossil”, such as petroleum coke or waste fossil fuels) have no verified free upstream factor (no free source prints one), so their upstream emissions are not quantified and the line is partial. Each line lists the fuels not mapped, the share of fossil heat input not mapped and the heat input not mapped that is attributable to the line (MMBtu, a memo outside every total). This is never treated as zero. (Coal is counted for mine methane only; see its own note.)
Included without a description of the activities the category covers.
Waste factors include transport to the treatment facility.

Some counted lines have no supporting evidence file linked (or only files that are missing or were rejected in review), so their figures rest on the entered data alone. The methodology gives the count.
Grid losses use location-based eGRID subregion rates.

More than one GWP basis is used in this Scope 3 total, including CO2e taken as reported by suppliers or other value-chain partners on their own declared basis, or as published by a factor source. Figures are not restated to one GWP set, so the total combines GWP bases; the GWP set of every figure is listed per record.

Upstream of natural gas (3A) multiplies the gas energy in MMBtu on a higher heating value basis, worked out exactly as for Scope 1, by NETL’s U.S. supply-chain intensity per MJ, which NETL states on the same higher heating value basis (production through distribution, 8.8 g CO2e/MJ).

The upstream of electricity from plants whose primary fuel is nuclear, biomass or a renewable source, where present in the subregion’s mix (the nuclear fuel cycle, harvesting, or the occasional fuel such plants burn), is never counted, so every upstream electricity line is partial. The company may document this as an exclusion within category 3. Gas co-fired at solar-thermal plants is fossil and has its own note.

Upstream of oil-fired generation uses CA-GREET3.0’s ultra-low sulfur diesel upstream (25.59 g CO2e/MJ, lower heating value) x CARB’s diesel energy density (134.47 MJ per gallon) / the EPA Hub distillate No. 2 heat content (0.138 MMBtu per gallon, higher heating value), 24.935415217391 kg CO2e per MMBtu: a proxy with uncertain direction for the residual and distillate oil power plants burn; their upstream boundaries differ from diesel. The two energy figures come from different sources: CARB’s lower heating value over EPA’s higher heating value gives a ratio of 0.924, against 0.928 for GREET’s own diesel pair, so the term is about 0.5% lower than a single-source conversion would give. eGRID’s oil category also includes petroleum coke and waste oil, whose upstream differs from refined diesel; the proxy is applied to them too.

Plants whose primary fuel eGRID records as “other fuel” (OTHF: for example waste heat, purchased steam, tyres or hydrogen) burn fuel with no upstream factor here. It is not assumed fossil; its upstream is not counted and the line is partial, with the heat input attributable to the line listed as a memo. This is never treated as zero.
Each power plant’s heat input is assigned to its primary fuel (eGRID PLFUELCT); fuel burned at a plant whose primary fuel is different is counted under that primary fuel.
Air travel excludes radiative forcing (non-CO2 effects at altitude).

Plants whose primary fuel is solar include solar-thermal plants that also burn natural gas. That gas is fossil, but its upstream is not counted here, so the line is partial; each line states this heat input (MMBtu, a memo outside every total). It is never treated as zero.

This category combines spend-based figures with figures from other methods (activity data, supplier or partner data). Each purchase must be counted once: check that no spend line covers something already recorded another way.
Some spend lines exclude sales tax. The amounts are used as recorded with EPA’s Supply Chain factors, which are per dollar of purchaser price (with margins) or producer price (without margins).
Some supplier figures have not been verified by a third party; unless the company rates them, their reliability is rated fair.
Some supplier figures are CO2e as the supplier reported it, with IPCC AR5 GWPs.
Transport, travel and commuting are tank-to-wheel: the upstream emissions of the fuels are not included.

The coal term of this upstream line is on IPCC AR5 100-year GWPs (EPA’s greenhouse gas inventory), while its natural gas term is on AR6 (NETL) and its oil term on inferred AR4 (CA-GREET3.0). Each line lists the GWP basis of every term; the terms are added as published, not restated.

NETL publishes its natural gas supply-chain intensities as CO2e with IPCC AR6 100-year GWPs (the AR5 results are in a separate appendix that could not be read), so these upstream figures are on AR6 while Scope 1 and 2 use AR5. They are used as published, not restated.

CARB does not state the GWP set of the CA-GREET3.0 carbon intensities; recomputing printed CA-GREET3.0 tables shows IPCC AR4 100-year values (CH4 25, N2O 298). These upstream figures are used as published, not restated.

Upstream of electricity (3B, 3C upstream, 3D upstream) uses eGRID2023 plant heat input, which is on a higher heating value basis (40 CFR 72.2 gross calorific value and the EIA gross heat content convention behind eGRID; the eGRID Technical Guide does not state it), matching NETL’s higher heating value basis.
Spend-based figures use U.S. national sector averages per dollar (EPA Supply Chain GHG Emission Factors v1.3), not the supplier’s own emissions.
